sources.title: Serverfarm: Clarksville ARK1 topping-out milestone and continuing construction, October 30, 2026
sources.summary: Serverfarm’s October 30 article reports that construction continues at its Clarksville data-centre campus. It separately dates placement of the final structural beam on ARK1, the first building, to October 7. The observation supports an under-construction campus anchored at ARK1; structural topping-out is not whole-building completion, commissioning or operation.

extraction.publication_date_basis: Visible October 30, 2026 and Article JSON-LD datePublished 2026-10-30T21:02:02+00:00; original WordPress post confirms October 30.
extraction.event_scope: Final structural beam on ARK1, the first building.
extraction.current_statement_basis: The dated article separately states that construction continues and that important work remains ahead.
extraction.successor_review: The operator’s complete latest 15 WordPress posts and original blog index were checked through November 11. The only later post, November 10, concerns a veteran’s career and contains no Clarksville status change. Current campus material still describes future completion of the first two buildings by January 2028. The municipal utility’s October 26 packet describes ongoing water-line relocation for Serverfarm; its October 30 packet discusses future capacity procurement, not energized IT capacity or operation. Targeted later-status searches located no later primary completion, operational, cancellation or pause statement. The separately discussed future power plant, bond referendum and utility procurement are not new data-centre hosts or physical completion evidence.

sources.title: Serverfarm ARK Clarksville campus: phased colocation development
sources.summary: The original operator campus page identifies the Clarksville development as ARK1–ARK4 and presents each building as colocation space. The page describes construction as underway and targets the first two buildings for January 2028. The page is undated, so retrieval does not set a physical-status date. Published building capacity, floor area, investment and completion targets remain plans, not commissioned capacity.

extraction.identity_scope: Operator’s own Clarksville campus page identifies ARK1, ARK2, ARK3 and ARK4; intended Serverfarm commercial colocation campus.
extraction.date_semantics: Undated live page; do not substitute copyright year, upload path or retrieval time for publication or physical event dates.
extraction.capacity_scope: Each building table lists 108 MW building capacity and 300,000 square feet on two floors. No commissioning, IT-load classification or delivered capacity is established. No numeric capacity is selected for admission.
extraction.factsheet_scope: Undated fact sheet, linked from operator page, describes a future campus, intended jobs and future dedicated generation. Conceptual renderings are explicitly marked subject to change. It notes a future December 1, 2026 bond vote; this is not a construction or commissioning date.

sources.title: FAA OE/AAA 2026-ASW-6954-OE: Ironwood Building ARK1, Clarksville
sources.summary: The original public FAA case names Ironwood Building ARK1 in Clarksville, Arkansas; identifies the Serverfarm Yates/Nabholz construction team; and describes land between Big Danger Road and Palmer Road immediately south of State Highway 123. The case publishes pointConverted.coordinate [-93.44001944, 35.45926667] with horizontalDatum WGS 84. This is a filed building point used as a campus anchor; the aviation no-hazard determination does not establish construction, completion, data-centre permitting or operation.

extraction.coordinate_treatment: Direct reuse of FAA’s explicitly labelled WGS 84 point, rounded to seven decimals. FAA names the field pointConverted but does not expose the original input datum, operation, realization or epoch in this response. No local datum conversion is performed or asserted.
extraction.identity_basis: structureName, city, locationDescription and sponsor/representative organization-address extension ATTN: SERVERFARM YATES/NABHOLZ JV are within the same original case record. Individual contact names, addresses, emails and phone numbers are not projected.
extraction.date_semantics: Publication date is unknown. Submitted timestamps and administrative no-hazard status are case metadata, not an observed physical construction event.
extraction.raw_api_access: Read-only public case lookup used by FAA’s published asn-case-display JavaScript. Request POST body retained with the capture.
extraction.independent_scope_limit: The coordinate identifies the filed ARK1 building point. It does not delineate a building footprint, entrance, surveyed boundary or total campus extent.

sources.title: Arkansas GIS Office parcel records for SF ARK1 LLC in Johnson County
sources.summary: The official statewide parcel response returns adjoining Johnson County parcels 002-01530-000 and 002-01630-000, both recorded to SF ARK1 LLC. The FAA ARK1 point falls within the latter, about 140 metres from its boundary. These records corroborate the physical identity and location of the filed building. They do not establish the entire campus boundary, current legal title after subsequent transactions or a new construction-status observation.

extraction.source_crs: EPSG:26915, NAD83 / UTM zone 15N, published by layer and query response.
extraction.selected_role: Identity and spatial corroboration only; no parcel-derived point is selected.
extraction.coordinate_comparison: For containment only, the published FAA WGS 84 point was inversely represented through EPSG:1188 (NAD83 to WGS 84 (1), zero translations, 4 m nominal operation accuracy) and projected to UTM 15N using pyproj 3.8.0 / PROJ 9.8.1. The point is about 140 m inside parcel 002-01630-000. This approximate comparison does not alter the admitted FAA point or establish total location accuracy. Full operation and software metadata are retained in the derived review JSON.
extraction.limitations: AGISO describes approximate cadastral locations and a publication snapshot of county assessment records. Two taxarea attributes total about 135 acres; geometrically calculated areas differ, and neither is used as campus size.

sources.title: Teraco CT1 expansion announcement, original publication November 12, 2025
sources.license: publisher-source-terms; compact factual projection only; no open-content licence asserted
sources.summary: The original operator release dates its announcement to November 12, 2025. It separately describes existing CT1 Rondebosch hosting services and the expansion underway, with early-2027 completion forecast. July 17, 2026 is explicitly webpage modification metadata, not a new physical-status observation.

extraction.scope: The original article distinguishes existing CT1 hosting services from the separate expansion under construction. Each observation applies only to its own project at the same host; existing operation does not establish expansion completion.

planned_expansion_power.scope: Additional critical IT load for the CT1 expansion only. The existing selected amount, range, stage, method, confidence and notes are preserved; only its unsupported observation date and evidence binding are corrected. This is not operating load, measured consumption or commissioned capacity.

extraction.date_review: Article and WebPage JSON-LD, Open Graph publication metadata, visible heading date and body dateline agree on November 12, 2025. The separately labelled July 17, 2026 modification time cannot refresh construction status. The original news index also lists the article under November 12, 2025.
extraction.forecast_limit: Early-2027 completion remains a forecast. No completion, operation or commissioned expansion capacity is inferred.

sources.title: Teraco: Powering Africa’s digital future from the heart of Teraco, May 30, 2025
sources.license: publisher-source-terms; compact factual projection only; no open-content licence asserted
sources.summary: The dated operator article explicitly states that Teraco operates eight data centres and then names the Isando JB1/JB3/JB5 campus, Bredell JB2/JB4 and Durban DB1 among its physical facilities. It describes existing interconnection/colocation services and, for DB1, a completed earlier expansion. This supports operation of those existing hosts as of the article date; it does not date individual hall openings or customer commissioning.
